transcript.content: Hello. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, doctor. Thank you for seeing me. Um, I hope I'm doing this right, but my family thought it would be a good idea for me to talk to someone. I've been under a bit of stress, I guess. Is it okay if I just explain a little bit about what's going on? 

It's... well, it's about my father's passing. I know everyone keeps telling me the hospital records and the donation emails all line up perfectly, and I really don't want to be difficult or cause any trouble for anyone. I know how that sounds. But... I'm a systems analyst, so I look at data all day, and when I compare the timestamps, the missing attachments, and the way certain community members just sort of avoid my questions... it’s obvious to me that someone is hiding what really happened around his death. I just want to understand the truth, you know? Does that make sense?
Have you ever heard voices, whispers, or sounds that other people couldn't hear?

Oh, um... no. No, nothing like that. I know why you're asking, and I completely understand, but... no. I've never heard voices or whispers or anything that wasn't actually there. 

I promise I'm not... I mean, I hope you don't think my mind is playing tricks on me in that way. Everything I'm looking at is just right there on the screen in the data. I'm completely normal when it comes to hearing things, I swear. Does that answer your question okay?
Aside from the stress about this situation, have you been feeling persistently down, sad, or hopeless lately?

Oh, no. No, I wouldn't say that. I mean, sure, it's a little stressful trying to piece everything together, but... no, I don't feel hopeless or persistently sad at all. I actually try to stay pretty positive. I still go to work every day and do my job just fine, and I still enjoy the things I normally enjoy. 

I really hope I'm not coming across as a negative person or anything. I just want to get to the bottom of the data, but otherwise, my mood is totally fine. I'm handling it okay, I promise. Is that... does that answer what you were looking for?
Before your father passed away, did you generally find it difficult to trust other people?

Oh, um, no, not at all. I've always been a pretty trusting person, honestly. I've always had good relationships with my coworkers and friends, and I like to think I see the best in people. 

I really don't want you to think I'm just... naturally suspicious or paranoid or anything like that. That's not me at all. Before all this happened with the hospital data, I never had any reason to doubt anyone. It's just this one specific situation where the numbers don't add up, you know? But generally speaking, I'm very easy to get along with and I trust people just fine. I hope that makes sense?

latest_inference.note: Patient denies lifelong pervasive mistrust prior to this specific event, ruling out Paranoid Personality Disorder (F60.0). Absence of hallucinations, thought disorder, or functional deterioration also rules out Schizophrenia (F20.0), leaving Delusional Disorder (F22).
